svg.title: Lesson 0002 overview: How YOLO produces predictions
svg.desc: A portrait hand-drawn technical lesson overview with twelve numbered stations showing how the current YOLOv5 fused-decode tensor changes from 640 by 640 input into final cube detections.
svg.text: From a 640×640 tensor to final cube boxes
Read the numbered stations 1 → 12. The center ribbon shows the data flow.

g.text: one forward pass → many candidate rows
three detection scales, not 8400 final boxes
Now each row is one candidate
[cx, cy, w, h, blue, green, red]
one model output → fewer, usable boxes
best class score and class ID
The model proposes; the decoder interprets.
left = cx − w/2, top = cy − h/2,
right = cx + w/2, bottom = cy + h/2.
Keep a row only when its best
then clip to the original frame.
resize + pad; return ratio and pad
Current implementation: confidence and NMS happen before the later geometry check.
best.onnx / best.engine use the fused-decode layout [1, 7, 8400].
Generic YOLO examples may show a different tensor; read this artifact first.
The lesson explains this implementation—not every possible YOLO export.

svg.text: MENTAL MODEL: propose many → interpret rows → keep strong classes → restore coordinates → suppress duplicates
Teaching examples are illustrative; the tensor shape and code path are project facts.
LESSON 0002 · READ THE OUTPUT BEFORE YOU TRUST THE BOX
